Package neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline.twophasepipe.closure

Class SlugUnitModel

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline.twophasepipe.closure.SlugUnitModel
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class SlugUnitModel extends Object implements Serializable
Steady slug-unit closure for gas-liquid intermittent flow.

A slug unit is an aerated liquid slug followed by a film zone in which a liquid film runs under (or, in steep upward flow, around) an elongated gas bubble. The unit travels at the translational velocity vT. Following Dukler and Hubbard (1975) and the equilibrium-film simplification of Taitel and Barnea (1990), the film holdup is the root of the combined gas-film momentum balance written with velocities fixed by mass conservation relative to the moving slug front. The slug fraction then follows from the unit liquid balance.

The pressure gradient charges mixture wall friction to the slug body only and per-phase wall friction to the film zone, plus gravity. In the frame moving with the slug front the unit is periodic, so the momentum flux entering a unit equals the flux leaving it and the unit-averaged gradient is wall friction plus gravity (Taitel and Barnea 1990). Dukler and Hubbard (1975) add the acceleration of the film liquid picked up at the slug front; that term is reported in SlugUnitModel.Result.accelerationGradient. How much of it is counted in SlugUnitModel.Result.frictionGradient is set with setFrontMixingLossWeight(double) or setFrontMixingLossIncluded(boolean); by default an OLGA-calibrated weight is used that is zero on slopes steeper than about 2 degrees and below Froude number 2.3. Benchmarking against OLGA 2025.1 on a 10 in gas-oil line showed why: on a horizontal section wall shear alone gives 61 Pa/m against 86 in OLGA and the front term (14 Pa/m) closes part of the gap, but on 4 degree up-slopes wall shear plus gravity (229 Pa/m) already matches OLGA (233 Pa/m) and the front term there (135 Pa/m) is pure excess.

The unit holdup follows from the liquid balance as hs + (vB/vt)(1 - hs) - vsG/vt, independent of the film balance, so the slip of the whole unit is set by the translational velocity vt and the bubble velocity vB. A 32-case OLGA 2025.1 steady sweep (8 to 16 in gas-oil, gas-oil-water, gas-condensate and wet-gas lines, 30 to 100 bara) showed the Bendiksen value vt = 1.2 vm overstates the slip above Froude number 3: OLGA's unit gas velocity falls from 1.25 vm at Froude 2 to about 1.12 - 0.25 vsL/vm times vm above Froude 4.5. Both velocities are therefore scaled towards no-slip by setHighFroudeSlipReductionEnabled(boolean) (on by default, horizontal sections only), which removed a 20 to 40 per cent holdup over-prediction and gives the thinner film (about 0.11 to 0.19) and larger slug fraction OLGA carries. When slugs cannot be sustained (slug fraction at or below zero) the result is flagged SlugUnitModel.Result.stratified; when the film vanishes the unit degenerates to the slug body.

Closures: slug-body holdup of Gregory, Nicholson and Aziz (1978); translational velocity of Bendiksen (1984); dispersed-bubble velocity in the slug body with a Harmathy rise term; stable slug length of 32 D horizontal and 16 D vertical (Barnea and Brauner 1985); Haaland wall friction; a constant interfacial Fanning factor of 0.014 in the film zone (Taitel and Barnea 1990).

    • automaticFrontMixingWeight

      static double automaticFrontMixingWeight(double froude, double sinTheta)
      Horizontal front-mixing weight calibrated against OLGA 2025.1.

      Wall shear alone under-predicts the OLGA unit gradient on horizontal gas-oil lines at moderate Froude number (65 against 83 Pa/m at Froude 3.4) and the front term closes it, but on up-slopes wall shear plus gravity already matches and the term is excess, so the weight is zero beyond about 2 degrees. It falls from 0.6 to 0.2 as the Froude number rises from 4.5 to 7 because the unit approaches no-slip and the pickup loss weakens.

      Parameters:
      froude - mixture Froude number vm / sqrt(g D)
      sinTheta - sine of the pipe inclination
      Returns:
      weight between zero and one

    • highFroudeSlipScale

      private double highFroudeSlipScale(double froude, double liquidFraction, double cosTheta)
      Scale factor on the translational and bubble velocities at high mixture Froude number.

      Bendiksen's distribution coefficient of 1.2 is a developed-turbulent-profile value for the elongated bubble. In a horizontal or near-horizontal line the gas-liquid velocity ratio of the whole unit falls towards the no-slip limit as the mixing rate rises. OLGA 2025.1 steady runs on 8 to 12 in gas-oil, gas-oil-water and gas-condensate lines (mixture Froude number 2 to 7, liquid fraction 0.1 to 0.5) give a unit gas velocity of 1.25 vm near Froude 2, and about 1.12 - 0.25 liquid fraction times vm above Froude 4.5, against 1.2 vm without this scaling. The scaling is applied with cos(theta) squared so a vertical slug unit keeps the Nicklin value.

      Parameters:
      froude - mixture Froude number vm / sqrt(g D)
      liquidFraction - no-slip liquid fraction vsL / vm
      cosTheta - cosine of the pipe inclination
      Returns:
      scale factor in (0, 1]
